tool_args.old_string: \looseness=-2 Paired improvements ($\tau$-gated vs.\ VLA-only) reach statistical significance on Spatial with extended seeds (Appendix~\ref{sec:8seed}) but do not reach significance on other suites at the default seed count. Our finding is established for the tested lightweight MLP-based CRM; whether larger correction architectures or online fine-tuning would change this conclusion remains open. The method requires stochastic action diversity from the base VLA; deterministic models produce vacuous multi-sample signals (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}), establishing an architectural boundary. The CRM is trained on $K{=}10$ argmin-selected actions but deployed at $K{=}2$, creating a distribution shift that may limit correction quality; matched-$K$ training is a natural extension. The threshold $\tau$ is suite-dependent (Appendix~\ref{sec:tau_sweep}), recovery on $\pi_{0.5}$ is partial (Appendix, Table~\ref{tab:tau_sweep_pi05}), and all experiments use the LIBERO simulation benchmark; whether the degradation--recovery pattern transfers to other simulation environments, real-robot deployment with visual domain shift, or task domains beyond tabletop manipulation remains untested.

tool_args.old_string: \looseness=-1 The suite-level pattern reflects task-specific uncertainty structure. Spatial tasks require precise placement relative to landmarks; when the VLA hesitates about spatial relations, its flow-matching process produces genuinely diverse action candidates, and the CRM resolves this ambiguity productively. Object tasks involve novel instances where pretrained visuomotor representations transfer well, yielding confident predictions that correction can only perturb. Long is the most informative case: the VLA is largely confident (trigger ${\sim}$4\%), but the CRM---trained exclusively on shorter suites---is out-of-distribution, so the few corrections it applies are unreliable. This explains the residual $-$1.3\,pp gap despite aggressive gating and suggests that gating effectiveness depends jointly on VLA uncertainty calibration and CRM in-distribution coverage.
tool_args.new_string: \looseness=-2 The suite-level pattern reflects task-specific uncertainty structure. Spatial tasks require precise placement relative to landmarks, producing genuinely diverse candidates when the VLA hesitates; the CRM resolves this ambiguity productively. Object tasks involve novel instances where pretrained representations generalize well, yielding confident predictions that correction can only perturb. Long---where the CRM is out-of-distribution---confirms that gating effectiveness depends jointly on VLA uncertainty quality and CRM coverage.

Our pipeline detects \emph{when correction would hurt}, using calibrated gating to suppress correction on confident steps.
